extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and educated readers interested in standards of poetic composition and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing, reading, and criticizing poetry—focusing on diction, imagery, simile, unity of meaning, the discipline required for verse, and proper modes of critical response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between manufactured poems and works of genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Of all modes of literature, the manufacturing of poems demands the least talent or information; the difference between these and the works of genius is not less than between an egg and an egg-shell; yet at a distance they both look alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of superficially polished or manufactured verse that may imitate the surface of genius; look for deep originality and intellectual substance rather than mere outward resemblance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine collective meaning, not only separate images
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers often receive pleasure from the separate images and phrases successively, without asking themselves whether the collective meaning was sense or nonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a poem, check whether the images and phrases cohere into a sensible collective meaning. Example/anti-pattern: admiring lines word-by-word while the combined sense is absurd (as illustrated by certain admired lines that, taken together, may not make sense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise position and choice of words (diction and sentence-level craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost faultless position and choice of words in Pope's original compositions; analysis sentence by sentence and almost word by word is valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to word order, syntax, and precise lexical choice. Close, line/ sentence-level analysis reveals craft and is a valid basis for critical judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve the visual likeness in simile and avoid literalizing metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: In Spenser and Fletcher the thought is justifiable; the images are at least consistent. By contrast, in some translations the Dog Star is turned into a real dog, and the whole visual likeness is lost while the likeness in the effects is exaggerated into absurdity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good simile preserves the intended visual or imagistic likeness. Anti-pattern: transforming a figurative image into a literal absurdity (e.g., 'Dog Star' rendered as an actual dog breathing plagues), which destroys the simile's power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bombast and extravagant exaggeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Not to mention the tremendous bombast — the exaggeration renders the likeness in the effects absurd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive exaggeration or rhetorical inflation (bombast) undermines the image and makes poetry ridiculous rather than sublime. Strive for proportion and restraint in figurative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between image and intended effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The visual likeness is lost while the likeness in the effects is rendered absurd by the exaggeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that imagery and the effects they are meant to convey are consistent; do not sacrifice visual truth for hyperbolic consequences that contradict the image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty and delicacy of verse mechanics; necessity of long practice
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no profession on earth which requires an attention so early, so long, or so unintermitting as that of poetry; how difficult and delicate a task even the mere mechanism of verse is may be conjectured from the failure of those who have attempted poetry late in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that mastery of poetic form and metre usually requires early, continuous, and concentrated practice; evaluate late attempts with the understanding of this technical difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devotion and protective interest in one's intellectual offspring
rubrics_metrics.description: What of all that relates to himself and his family...can have fairer claims to his protection, or more authorize acts of self-defence, than the elaborate products of his intellect and intellectual industry?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should take a due interest in protecting and defending their works (as their 'offspring'); lack of concern for publication, sale, or reputation is not a mark of deserved neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance sensibility with rapidity of association in genius
rubrics_metrics.description: Profound sensibility is one component of genius, but a more than usual rapidity of association...is a component equally essential; in the due modification of each by the other the genius itself consists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a poet's greatness, look for both deep feeling (sensibility) and the mental agility that binds thoughts and images; one without the other may be pathological or deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensibility should not be primarily self-interested
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not less an essential mark of true genius, that its sensibility is excited by any other cause more powerfully than by its own personal interests; the man of genius lives most in the ideal world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine poetic sensibility is directed toward ideas, the past or future, and universal concerns rather than narrowly toward personal grievance or self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticize and oppose pretensions in full public argument (books), not in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: If I should ever deem it my duty at all to oppose the pretensions of individuals, I would oppose them in books which could be weighed and answered...not in irrecoverable conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging in critical dispute, present comprehensive, documented arguments in durable public form (books, essays) so reasons can be weighed and answered; avoid ephemeral conversation as a forum for sustained critical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of appeals to malignant passions as a route to popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Bunglers...have been able to drive a successful trade...by that most powerful of all adulation, the appeal to the bad and malignant passions of mankind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate an author's merit independently of popularity gained by pandering to base passions; work that courts envy, malice, or personal scandal may achieve fleeting reputation but lacks lasting literary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close critical re-examination can increase appreciation despite revealing faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever pleasure I may have lost by the clearer perception of the faults in certain passages has been more than repaid to me by the additional delight with which I read the remainder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough critical scrutiny may expose defects but can deepen overall appreciation by highlighting stronger parts; criticism can be enriching rather than merely destructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting faults requires impartial strictness and re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: I had been induced to re-examine with impartial strictness Gray's celebrated Elegy...I had long before detected the defects in The Bard; but the Elegy I had considered as proof against all fair attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply impartial, strict re-examination even to celebrated works; do not let reputation shield a work from legitimate critique.
